body: Wednesday, March 26 2025 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto
Information available before 2025-03-26 00:00 UTC. Prices use completed prior sessions. Prepared retrospectively; later outcomes are excluded.

Macro Stance: Consumer confidence is breaking lower just as the tariff debate hardens. Reuters reports that rising fears of tariffs pulled US consumer confidence to a four-year low [1], and CNBC says the expectations gauge has fallen to a 12-year low [2]. Business Insider puts it bluntly: consumer sentiment is plunging, and Wall Street now sees a tired US shopper as a major risk to stocks [3]. Yahoo Finance says the data show no clear sign of a looming recession [4], yet a CNBC survey finds corporate CFOs pessimistic and expecting recession before the end of 2025 [5], and a Deutsche survey has the probability of recession approaching 50% [6]. Reuters frames the setup as stagflation risk, though without a repeat of the seventies [7].

Rates & Curve: The curve is positively sloped. The 10Y closed at 4.31% and the 2Y at 3.96%, a 10Y-2Y spread of +35 bps at the prior close (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-25). Over 20 observations the 2Y has fallen 11 bps while the 10Y has risen 1 bp, so the spread has widened 12 bps and the 20-observation move is labelled steepening (10Y up, 2Y down/flat). Over five observations the 2Y is down 8 bps and the 10Y up 2 bps. Reuters flags convexity risk after the recent Treasury yield decline [8], and Fortune’s line that ‘Don’t fight Bessent’s Treasury’ has become the bond-market mantra [9] describes a market that has been content to buy the front end. The S&P 500 closed at 5,776.65, up 0.16% in the prior session, up 2.89% over five sessions and down 3.00% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25; US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-25). The VIX closed at 17.15, down 20.97% over five sessions and down 11.73% over 20, and the dollar index sits at 104.18 index points, down 2.00% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25).

New / Most Important: The most important development is that the Fed is being pulled into the trade fight. The Hill reports Trump zeroing in on the Fed and setting up a potential fight with Powell [10], after Reuters reported that the Fed is in no rush to cut rates and that Trump disagrees [11]. The BBC says the Federal Reserve cut its US growth forecast as tariff fears increased [12], and Yahoo Finance quotes Powell linking trade to prices as the arrival of tariff inflation [13]. The front end still prices some easing, which is why the 2Y has slipped 11 bps over 20 observations.

Playbook ✓: Stay neutral on equity beta and keep duration in the belly of the curve rather than reaching for the long end, because the 10Y has risen while the 2Y rallies and the curve is steepening. Own cash-flow leaders that gain from tariff clarity rather than consumer-exposed names, and add index exposure only if the S&P 500 reclaims its 20-session reference of 5,955.25. The call turns Bearish if the VIX moves back above its 19.43 reference or the 10Y breaks above 4.31% with the curve still steepening. It turns Bullish if consumer confidence stabilises and the S&P 500 closes above 5,955.25.

Macro Stance: Europe is turning toward fiscal support. Germany’s landmark spending bill has won final lawmaker backing [14], and Bloomberg notes it reignites jitters over periphery debt [15], while the package is framed as a €1 trillion borrowing programme [16]. The activity signal is improving: the flash eurozone PMI points to a return to growth in manufacturing in March [17]. The weak spots are real. French private-sector output contracted further in March [18], and UK retail sales sank as confidence ebbed, the CBI says [19].

Activity & Inflation: The ECB is still data-dependent. Panetta says the ECB must be pragmatic and data driven in setting rates [20], and a decision on wider use of a favourable capital rule is still pending [21]. The Bank of England held rates at 4.5% [22] and warned that global trade uncertainty has intensified [23]. Reuters reports some European officials are weighing whether they can rely on the Fed for dollars under Trump [24], a funding question that matters more if transatlantic tension rises. EUR/USD closed at 1.0804, down 0.30% in the prior session and up 3.27% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25).

New / Most Important: The signal that matters is the rotation. SAP has overtaken Novo Nordisk as Europe’s largest company, Reuters reports [25], and Morningstar says the same [26]. SAP.DE closed at 258.75 EUR, up 4.88% over five sessions and down 5.01% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25), while NOVO-B.CO closed at 512.40 DKK, down 6.77% over five sessions and down 22.01% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Investors are moving money out of the US and into Europe, as Morningstar puts it [27].

Playbook ✓: Lean long European cyclicals and capital-goods names that benefit from German spending, and keep defensive pharma weight light while Novo is re-rating lower. Hedge euro exposure only if EUR/USD gives back the 20-session gain of 3.27%. The call changes if periphery spreads widen on the German plan [15] or if the ECB’s capital-rule decision [21] is read as a tighter stance.

Macro Stance: China is trying to convert stimulus into consumption, but deflation remains the binding constraint. An adviser urged lifting consumption to 70% of GDP by 2035 [28], and the WSJ says the stimulus is prompting cautious growth upgrades at global banks even as trade risks loom [29]. Morgan Stanley raised its Chinese stock targets again on earnings optimism [30]. The deflation evidence is still visible. China’s youth jobless rate rose to 16.9% in February [31], restaurants are racing to the bottom in a deflation-hit economy [32], and one economist says China needs more significant stimulus to crush deflation fears [33]. The policy direction is right; the price data have not caught up.

PMIs & Activity: The latest factory print is February’s, and Reuters reported that factory activity picked up while trade uncertainties weighed [34]. For the first two months of the year, industrial output rose 5.9%, beating market expectations [35], and retail sales were up 4% [36]. Those are the most recent activity prints available, and both are from mid-March. The view would be confirmed by a March factory reading that holds above 50 and by retail sales that keep improving on the back of the consumer push; a reading below 50 would confirm the deflation side of the argument instead.

Credit Impulse: The policy lever is the price of credit more than its quantity. Reuters reports the central bank will further erode the role of the medium-term loan rate [37], a step toward cheaper and more market-based financing for households and firms. The authorities are also leaning against froth: Hong Kong has ordered brokers to rein in credit to pre-empt IPO madness [38]. The bond market is ambiguous. Chinese bond yields are rising, but economists say deflation worries could soon pull them lower [39]. A turn in credit would show first in new loans; until then the view rests on policy direction.

Property: Property is still the swing factor. CNBC says China’s property market is edging toward an inflection point [40], but Reuters reports that the slump persists as stimulus struggles to stabilise the sector [41]. Some steelmakers have started output cuts in response to a national call [42], which is supply discipline rather than a demand recovery. Sunac is working on a second restructuring of its offshore debt [43]. Until new-home activity gives a clean signal, property is a drag on growth rather than a tailwind for it.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Policy is leaning toward consumers while the external fight escalates. Reuters reports a call to ramp up support for services consumption [44], and the WSJ reports China explores limiting its own exports to mollify Trump [45]. Export controls froze antimony shipments to the EU [46]. The external backdrop is harsh: the WSJ says the trade war is exploding across the world at a pace not seen in decades [47], and Southeast Asian stocks are feeling the heat [48]. Beijing is also building counter-tools, with new rules to step up countermeasures against foreign sanctions [49].

Markets & Flows: Chinese equities are not confirming the upgrade cycle. The Hang Seng closed at 23,344.25, down 2.35% in the prior session and down 5.64% over five sessions, though up 1.35% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). The Shanghai Composite closed at 3,369.98, down 1.74% over five sessions and up 0.72% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). The offshore internet proxy is weaker still: KWEB closed at 35.17 USD, down 7.03% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25), and the CSI 300 ETF ASHR at 26.87 USD is down 2.64% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Bloomberg reports signs of rotation from small caps to large in Chinese stocks [50]. USD/CNY sits at 7.2530, up 0.28% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25), so the currency is not signalling stress.

New / Most Important: The signal that matters most comes from China’s own tech leader. Alibaba’s chairman Joe Tsai warned of a bubble in the AI data-centre buildout [51] and said some AI bets, such as excess data centres, are speculative [52]. Reuters reports Alibaba is restarting hiring and sees signs of the start of an AI bubble in the US [53]. Ant Group’s claim that local GPUs cut AI model training costs by 20% [54] points to cost deflation in the sector. The tension for Chinese equities is that the policy upgrades are real, but the best-known private AI voice is warning about overbuilding, which argues against chasing the rally.

Playbook ✓: Stay Mixed. Prefer large-cap, policy-exposed names and the consumption theme over offshore internet and small caps until the Hang Seng holds its 20-session reference close of 23,034.02. The call turns Bullish if new loans and retail sales keep improving and the factory print holds above 50. It turns Bearish if the factory reading slips below 50 while the Hang Seng loses its reference level. ⚠ Divergence: the Morgan Stanley target raise [30] and the WSJ growth upgrades [29] point up, while the Hang Seng is down 5.64% over five sessions and KWEB is down 7.03% over the same span.

Macro Stance: Japan is tightening into a tariff shock. The BOJ kept rates steady and warned of Trump tariff risks [55], yet core inflation at 3% in February keeps alive bets on a rate hike [56]. The yield signal is clear: Japan’s 10-year yield has hit a 16½-year high [57], and Governor Ueda has said the BOJ has been gradually tapering its long-term JGB holdings [58]. Households feel the squeeze, slashing cash at a record pace as inflation bites [59]. Toyota, the bellwether exporter, was bullish on Trump until the tariff threats arrived [60].

Activity & Currency: USD/JPY closed at 150.7740, up 0.73% in the prior session and up 0.61% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). The yen has weakened even as a Japanese lawmaker says it is undervalued and wants steps to reverse outflows [61]. The Nikkei 225 closed at 37,780.54, up 1.03% over five sessions but down 2.57% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Chip tooling faces a new challenger, with China’s SiCarrier emerging against ASML and other chip-tool titans [62], and Tokyo Electron is down 12.36% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). SoftBank is still spending into AI, buying Ampere Computing for $6.5 billion [63], yet its shares are down 12.32% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25).

Playbook ✓: Underweight yen-sensitive exporters with tariff exposure, and keep the long end of the JGB curve light while the 10-year sits at a 16½-year high [57]. Yen longs work only as a hedge. The call turns Mixed if USD/JPY closes back under its 20-session reference of 149.86 and the Nikkei reclaims its 20-session reference of 38,776.94. It turns Bullish on Japanese equities only if the tapering and the rate-hike bets stop pushing yields up faster than earnings can absorb.

Macro Stance: Australia is describing a soft landing. ABC reports the budget papers say the economy is on track for a ‘soft landing’ [64], and the federal budget leans on households, with Centrelink support for 460,000 pensioners in a $450 million move [65]. Public employment is still growing, with Labor adding 3,400 public service roles [66], even as a clothing retailer’s collapse cost hundreds of jobs [67] and a university cut up to 180 more jobs as student visa changes bite [68].

Demand & Financing: AUD/USD closed at 0.6286, down 1.51% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). The S&P/ASX 200 closed at 7,942.50, up 1.04% over five sessions but down 3.75% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Banks are the swing. CBA closed at 148.63 AUD, down 3.66% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25), and an S&P Global piece says the stock may drop 23% as analysts flag overvaluation [69]. Housing support is coming through policy: the government is expanding a first-home-buyer scheme as an election looms [70], and Labor will lift the income and price caps [71]. On the resource side, iron ore miners are in the spotlight as Chinese demand rises [72], while BHP closed at 39.04 AUD, down 3.15% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25).

Playbook ✓: Stay Mixed. Fund any rally with resource names that confirm the iron-ore bid rather than with the big banks, which look stretched on the analyst warning [69]. CBA would need to reclaim its 20-session reference of 154.27 AUD before the bank call turns Bullish. Keep AUD exposure hedged until AUD/USD recovers through its 20-session reference of 0.6338. The call turns Bullish if the ASX 200 holds its five-session gain and the Help to Buy changes [71] start to show up in housing demand.

Macro Stance: Poland’s central bank is cautious and divided. Money.pl reports the NBP votes show Glapiński cannot count on unanimity [73], and Parkiet says the NBP sees inflation within target by mid-2026 while the market expects that much sooner [74]. The NBP is also adding to its reserves, with more tonnes of gold in the vault [75]. Activity is soft. Industrial output fell 2.0% year on year in February, according to GUS [76], and ING expects output to recover more slowly than forecast [77]. Household incomes keep rising [78], and unemployment is up, though fewer people are out of work than estimated, Business Insider Polska reports [79]. Dozens of firms announced group layoffs in a single month, TVN24 reports [80]. The finance ministry relays that Moody’s credited the strong dynamics of the Polish economy and better relations with the EU [81].

Markets: Polish equities have run hard over 20 sessions. The WIG20 total-return tracker closed at 53.18 PLN, up 8.84% over 20 sessions, and the EPOL ETF closed at 29.11 USD, up 12.18% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Leadership sits in banks and energy: PKO Bank Polski at 78.70 PLN is up 14.16% over 20 sessions, Orlen at 69.90 PLN is up 15.25%, and mBank at 864.20 PLN is up 18.22% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). LPP, the apparel retailer, is down 0.39% over 20 sessions at 17,980.00 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25), so the consumer names have not joined the rally. USD/PLN closed at 3.8639, down 2.43% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25), so the zloty has firmed. The WIG20 is attacking 2800 points [82], and the index is being reshaped toward consumer names [83]. Bankier reports that capital on the Warsaw exchange has reached levels it had never seen before [84].

Fiscal & Politics: Fiscal pressure is the policy risk. Business Insider Polska reports public debt has broken another barrier [85], and the 2024 budget outturn showed Belka-tax revenue rising [86]. Banks are the revenue target. Rzeczpospolita asks whether banks, the budget’s golden-egg hen, should be taxed even more [87], and Money.pl reports the minister wants to get at the banks’ windfall while the sector protests [88]. The government has also approved a bill to boost spending on social housing [89]. The ratings backdrop is the offset: the finance ministry says Moody’s appreciated the economy’s strength [81].

Corporate & Sectors: Banks, energy and defence lead the corporate story. The Warsaw Stock Exchange’s core profit rose on record revenue growth, Reuters reports [90], and Alior Bank has set out a strategy to 2027 [91]. Bank dividends for 2025 are being listed [92]. PGE plans large storage spending, with a headline calling the Żarnowiec project the largest in Europe [93], and PGE closed at 8.29 PLN, up 17.59% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Orlen is hunting for gas and oil overseas, which Bankier calls practically unlimited resources [94], and Orlen has received 1.7 billion zloty of European Investment Bank funding for grid development [95]. CD Projekt says The Witcher 4 will come after 2026 [96], and the shares closed at 229.70 PLN, up 5.76% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). KGHM is spending billions on new mine shafts [97], with the stock at 140.75 PLN, up 5.83% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25).

Geopolitics & Security: Defence is the growth story that policy keeps reinforcing. Bankier reports the defence industry is hiring heavily [98], Money.pl says the sector is trying to widen a production bottleneck [99], and the state defence group wants to win abroad [100]. Poland has asked NATO to raise the minimum defence spending to 3% of GDP [101], Donald Tusk has announced military training for all men [102], and Poland and the Baltic states plan to quit the landmine treaty over Russia fears [103]. On Ukraine, Russia and Ukraine agreed a naval ceasefire in the Black Sea [104], but Moscow set far-reaching conditions for implementing it [105]. The regional security premium stays on, which keeps defence-linked names in favour.

New / Most Important: The signal that matters most is that the zloty is strong while the factory side is weak. The zloty hit a 10-year high against the dollar on a hawkish central bank in late February [106], and USD/PLN closed at 3.8639 in the prior session, down 2.43% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). That gives the NBP room to keep policy restrictive while output falls 2.0% year on year [76]. For equities, rate-sensitive banks carry the rally, and the bank tax debate [87] is the risk that could reverse that leadership.

Playbook ✓: Stay Bullish on banks, energy and defence, but size bank exposure through the WIG20 total-return tracker rather than one name, because the tax debate [88] can move quickly. Keep the zloty long only while USD/PLN stays under its 20-session reference of 3.9599. Dino Polska at 455.80 PLN, down 7.19% over five sessions, is the consumer-side warning. The call turns Mixed if the bank tax moves from debate into legislation, or if inflation tracks the market’s earlier timetable rather than the NBP’s mid-2026 view [74]. ⚠ Divergence: the WIG20 is attacking 2800 [82] and the zloty is firm, while industrial output fell 2.0% year on year in February [76].

Narrative: Technology is the consensus AI trade, but the group is running into valuation fatigue. XLK closed at 218.35, up 2.92% over five sessions and down 4.45% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Morgan Stanley’s Mike Wilson sees beaten-up megacap names as the near-term winners [107], which is a rotation call inside tech rather than a call on the whole sector.

Reported: Micron’s print was solid, but the stock fell: Barron’s says the detail that overshadowed the results pulled shares lower [108]. MU closed at 94.18 USD, down 7.41% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Nvidia’s earnings beat drew a shrug from investors, S&P Global reports [109], so beats are not being rewarded at the top of the group.

EPS Upside Watch: Broadcom has the most demand momentum among the chip names, with Forbes asking how high the AI boom can take the chipmaker [110]. AVGO closed at 188.26 USD, down 7.05% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25), so an upside surprise would have a low bar to clear on price.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The convention says AI capex is a supercycle, but the loudest voice from China’s largest cloud and commerce group warns of bubble risk. Alibaba’s chairman says there are signs of an AI bubble forming in the US [53] and warned of a bubble in the AI data-centre buildout [51]. Quantum-computing stocks are falling as Jensen Huang and other CEOs temper expectations [111]. The sector’s 20-session drawdown is the market already pricing that doubt.

Narrative: Communication services is holding up on the platform and advertising story. XLC closed at 99.94, up 4.20% over five sessions and down 1.72% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Meta is weighing a paid, ad-free option in the UK [112], a sign the platform is testing new revenue streams, and Google is searching for an answer to ChatGPT [113], which keeps the AI-competition debate at the centre of the group.
Reported: The sector’s news is deal flow: Google’s $32 billion Wiz deal may signal a turning point for slow IPO and M&A markets, CNBC reports [114].

EPS Upside Watch: The watch is on advertising-linked platforms and on the deal pipeline. GOOGL closed at 170.56 USD, up 6.16% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25), and the Wiz deal is the cleanest catalyst for upside in estimates if integration costs stay contained.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The convention says a slowing ad market hurts platforms, yet Alphabet is up 6.16% over five sessions while the group is still lower over 20. Cathie Wood’s sale of Meta shares for the first time in nearly a year [115] is a reminder that even long-term holders trim platform names when the story gets crowded. The tension is between the five-session bounce and the 20-session drift.

Narrative: Financials are carried by the curve and by deal flow. The curve is positively sloped with a 10Y-2Y spread of +35 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-25), which supports net interest margins as it steepens. XLF closed at 50.43, up 2.86% over five sessions and down 1.04% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Bloomberg reports banks are preparing a €2.5 billion bond sale for Flutter’s Italy deal [116], a sign the debt market is open for large transactions.

Reported: Morgan Stanley is cutting 2,000 jobs but sparing its wealth managers, Barron’s reports [117], which is a cost story rather than a revenue one. MS closed at 125.20 USD, up 6.00% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Axos Financial topped the 2024 ranking of US public banks over $10B in assets, S&P Global reports [118].

EPS Upside Watch: The upside is in trading and capital-markets revenue after a volatile stretch. JPMorgan closed at 251.13 USD, up 6.88% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25), and Goldman Sachs at 585.94 USD, up 6.19% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25), so some of the rebound is already in the price. The advisory side is the laggard: billions raised by perennially private firms keep IPOs on ice [119].

⚡ Breaking Convention: The convention says banks lose when recession fears rise, yet the big banks are up more than 6% over five sessions while the sector is still lower over 20. The policy risk cuts across the trade: Semafor reports Treasury’s play for regulatory control puts it on a collision course with the Fed [120].

Narrative: Energy is trading the Venezuela tariff threat against a Russia-Ukraine truce. XLE closed at 93.23, up 2.07% over five sessions and up 4.00% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Reuters says oil prices are mixed as the Russia-Ukraine truce offsets Venezuela supply worries [121], and WTI closed at 69.00 USD, up 3.14% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25).

Reported: Sinopec’s full-year profit slumped as headwinds mounted, Bloomberg reports [122], and Shell plans more cost and spending cuts while handing its chief executive a bigger bonus [123]. XOM closed at 116.59 USD, up 6.25% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25), so the majors have held up better than the reports suggest.

EPS Upside Watch: The upside is in the cost-cutting majors and in refiners that benefit from wider margins. The cleanest way to be wrong is a Russian supply deal. Traders say the route back for Russian energy is long [124], which limits how much sanction relief can add to earnings in the near term.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The convention is that Venezuela tariffs lift crude. Reuters reports Venezuelan oil loadings are slowing amid US tariffs and a licence termination [125], and China’s purchases have stalled after the tariff threat [126]. That is a supply squeeze on paper that has not yet shown up as a price surge: WTI is up 3.14% over five sessions but barely changed over 20.

Narrative: Industrials are a defence-and-infrastructure story with a tariff hangover. XLI closed at 134.49, up 1.98% over five sessions and down 0.32% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Germany’s landmark spending bill has won final backing [14], and chip companies have filed €6 billion of subsidy requests in Germany [127], a signal for European capex rather than an order book.

Reported: Boeing is cutting jobs in India, a headline says [128], even as its defence side wins: WSJ reports Boeing gets a lifeline in a Pentagon deal to build the most expensive jet fighter ever [129]. BA closed at 182.59 USD, up 13.01% over five sessions and up 2.42% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25).

EPS Upside Watch: The upside is in defence procurement and in European suppliers moving into defence. German suppliers are exploring defence opportunities, Automotive News reports [130], and private-equity defence investment is surging in early 2025, S&P Global says [131]. Those are demand signals rather than estimate revisions, so the earnings case depends on contract timing.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The convention says defence is the safe industrial, but Lockheed Martin is down 5.80% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25) while Boeing is up 13.01%. The market is separating the names that win contracts from those carrying legacy costs. Anduril’s plan for a UK drone factory [132] shows new entrants chasing the same European budgets.

Narrative: Discretionary is where tariffs and confidence meet. XLY closed at 205.92, up 6.42% over five sessions but down 4.86% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25), a bounce inside a downtrend. Business Insider says consumer sentiment is plunging [3], and retailers are bulking up inventories to blunt the tariff impact [133], which defers the price pain rather than removing it.

Reported: Nike expects sales will plunge in the current quarter as it faces tariffs and sliding consumer confidence [134], and its stock fell as the company joined what Fortune calls a growing list of tariff casualties [135]. NKE closed at 66.54 USD, down 9.23% over five sessions and down 18.58% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Kingfisher’s shares dived on a subdued profit outlook [136].

EPS Upside Watch: Upside is hard to find. The discretionary names with positive momentum have specific catalysts: Tesla’s rebound on Musk’s return [137] and Carvana testing new-vehicle sales in Arizona [138]. The EPS watch is about pricing power, and Nike’s guidance is the cautionary example of what tariffs do to it.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The convention says consumers trade down while experiences hold up. Olive Garden’s parent shrugged off concerns about plummeting confidence, saying diners keep treating themselves [139], which is the contrarian data point.

Narrative: Staples are not doing the defensive job they usually do. XLP closed at 78.68, down 1.34% over five sessions and down 5.89% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Yahoo Finance asks whether Procter & Gamble is the best defensive stock amid market volatility [140], but the group is lagging in the same tape where discretionary names bounced.

Reported: McCormick missed quarterly profit estimates on higher expenses [141]. Nestlé is closing two German plants by 2026 amid rising costs and declining sales [142]. Walmart was sliding, per Yahoo Finance [143], and WMT closed at 84.76 USD, down 13.24% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25).

EPS Upside Watch: Upside sits with names where input costs are contained or pricing is holding. Input costs are the swing factor for the group, so the watch is on cost language in company guidance. McCormick’s expense problem is the cautionary example [141], and the Nestlé plant closures show the cost side of the squeeze [142].

⚡ Breaking Convention: The convention says staples are the shelter in a confidence slump, but the group is down 5.89% over 20 sessions while cyclicals bounce over five. GameStop's plan is the copy in this case: a meme name copying a treasury model, and a copy is easier to repeat than the original. The mechanism that matters is the wrapper. geo.label: hold / data dependent
parts: Macro Stance

Consumer confidence is breaking lower just as the tariff debate hardens. Reuters reports that rising fears of tariffs pulled US consumer confidence to a four-year low [[n10100]], and CNBC says the expectations gauge has fallen to a 12-year low [[n10063]]. Business Insider puts it bluntly: consumer sentiment is plunging, and Wall Street now sees a tired US shopper as a major risk to stocks [[n8070]]. Yahoo Finance says the data show no clear sign of a looming recession [[n10430]], yet a CNBC survey finds corporate CFOs pessimistic and expecting recession before the end of 2025 [[n10451]], and a Deutsche survey has the probability of recession approaching 50% [[n10396]]. Reuters frames the setup as stagflation risk, though without a repeat of the seventies [[n10431]].
Rates & Curve

The curve is positively sloped. The 10Y closed at 4.31% and the 2Y at 3.96%, a 10Y-2Y spread of +35 bps at the prior close (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-25). Over 20 observations the 2Y has fallen 11 bps while the 10Y has risen 1 bp, so the spread has widened 12 bps and the 20-observation move is labelled steepening (10Y up, 2Y down/flat). Over five observations the 2Y is down 8 bps and the 10Y up 2 bps. Reuters flags convexity risk after the recent Treasury yield decline [[n10464]], and Fortune’s line that ‘Don’t fight Bessent’s Treasury’ has become the bond-market mantra [[n10349]] describes a market that has been content to buy the front end. The S&P 500 closed at 5,776.65, up 0.16% in the prior session, up 2.89% over five sessions and down 3.00% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25; US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-25). The VIX closed at 17.15, down 20.97% over five sessions and down 11.73% over 20, and the dollar index sits at 104.18 index points, down 2.00% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25).
New / Most Important

The most important development is that the Fed is being pulled into the trade fight. The Hill reports Trump zeroing in on the Fed and setting up a potential fight with Powell [[n10459]], after Reuters reported that the Fed is in no rush to cut rates and that Trump disagrees [[n10230]]. The BBC says the Federal Reserve cut its US growth forecast as tariff fears increased [[n10231]], and Yahoo Finance quotes Powell linking trade to prices as the arrival of tariff inflation [[n10214]]. The front end still prices some easing, which is why the 2Y has slipped 11 bps over 20 observations.
Playbook ✓

Stay neutral on equity beta and keep duration in the belly of the curve rather than reaching for the long end, because the 10Y has risen while the 2Y rallies and the curve is steepening. Own cash-flow leaders that gain from tariff clarity rather than consumer-exposed names, and add index exposure only if the S&P 500 reclaims its 20-session reference of 5,955.25. The call turns Bearish if the VIX moves back above its 19.43 reference or the 10Y breaks above 4.31% with the curve still steepening. It turns Bullish if consumer confidence stabilises and the S&P 500 closes above 5,955.25.

geo.label: fiscal impulse / growth turning up
parts: Macro Stance

Europe is turning toward fiscal support. Germany’s landmark spending bill has won final lawmaker backing [[n3074]], and Bloomberg notes it reignites jitters over periphery debt [[n3075]], while the package is framed as a €1 trillion borrowing programme [[n3077]]. The activity signal is improving: the flash eurozone PMI points to a return to growth in manufacturing in March [[n1276]]. The weak spots are real. French private-sector output contracted further in March [[n3150]], and UK retail sales sank as confidence ebbed, the CBI says [[n10115]].
Activity & Inflation

The ECB is still data-dependent. Panetta says the ECB must be pragmatic and data driven in setting rates [[n3202]], and a decision on wider use of a favourable capital rule is still pending [[n3065]]. The Bank of England held rates at 4.5% [[n2976]] and warned that global trade uncertainty has intensified [[n2983]]. Reuters reports some European officials are weighing whether they can rely on the Fed for dollars under Trump [[n3144]], a funding question that matters more if transatlantic tension rises. EUR/USD closed at 1.0804, down 0.30% in the prior session and up 3.27% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25).
New / Most Important

The signal that matters is the rotation. SAP has overtaken Novo Nordisk as Europe’s largest company, Reuters reports [[n3170]], and Morningstar says the same [[n3231]]. SAP.DE closed at 258.75 EUR, up 4.88% over five sessions and down 5.01% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25), while NOVO-B.CO closed at 512.40 DKK, down 6.77% over five sessions and down 22.01% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Investors are moving money out of the US and into Europe, as Morningstar puts it [[n3175]].
Playbook ✓

Lean long European cyclicals and capital-goods names that benefit from German spending, and keep defensive pharma weight light while Novo is re-rating lower. Hedge euro exposure only if EUR/USD gives back the 20-session gain of 3.27%. The call changes if periphery spreads widen on the German plan [[n3075]] or if the ECB’s capital-rule decision [[n3065]] is read as a tighter stance.

geo.label: stimulus building, deflation unresolved
parts: Macro Stance

China is trying to convert stimulus into consumption, but deflation remains the binding constraint. An adviser urged lifting consumption to 70% of GDP by 2035 [[n1346]], and the WSJ says the stimulus is prompting cautious growth upgrades at global banks even as trade risks loom [[n1351]]. Morgan Stanley raised its Chinese stock targets again on earnings optimism [[n1369]]. The deflation evidence is still visible. China’s youth jobless rate rose to 16.9% in February [[n9808]], restaurants are racing to the bottom in a deflation-hit economy [[n1185]], and one economist says China needs more significant stimulus to crush deflation fears [[n1083]]. The policy direction is right; the price data have not caught up.
PMIs & Activity

The latest factory print is February’s, and Reuters reported that factory activity picked up while trade uncertainties weighed [[n0602]]. For the first two months of the year, industrial output rose 5.9%, beating market expectations [[n1012]], and retail sales were up 4% [[n1035]]. Those are the most recent activity prints available, and both are from mid-March. The view would be confirmed by a March factory reading that holds above 50 and by retail sales that keep improving on the back of the consumer push; a reading below 50 would confirm the deflation side of the argument instead.
Credit Impulse

The policy lever is the price of credit more than its quantity. Reuters reports the central bank will further erode the role of the medium-term loan rate [[n1262]], a step toward cheaper and more market-based financing for households and firms. The authorities are also leaning against froth: Hong Kong has ordered brokers to rein in credit to pre-empt IPO madness [[n1194]]. The bond market is ambiguous. Chinese bond yields are rising, but economists say deflation worries could soon pull them lower [[n1146]]. A turn in credit would show first in new loans; until then the view rests on policy direction.
Property

Property is still the swing factor. CNBC says China’s property market is edging toward an inflection point [[n1141]], but Reuters reports that the slump persists as stimulus struggles to stabilise the sector [[n0996]]. Some steelmakers have started output cuts in response to a national call [[n1307]], which is supply discipline rather than a demand recovery. Sunac is working on a second restructuring of its offshore debt [[n1270]]. Until new-home activity gives a clean signal, property is a drag on growth rather than a tailwind for it.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

Policy is leaning toward consumers while the external fight escalates. Reuters reports a call to ramp up support for services consumption [[n1139]], and the WSJ reports China explores limiting its own exports to mollify Trump [[n1192]]. Export controls froze antimony shipments to the EU [[n1137]]. The external backdrop is harsh: the WSJ says the trade war is exploding across the world at a pace not seen in decades [[n1318]], and Southeast Asian stocks are feeling the heat [[n1308]]. Beijing is also building counter-tools, with new rules to step up countermeasures against foreign sanctions [[n3994]].
Markets & Flows

Chinese equities are not confirming the upgrade cycle. The Hang Seng closed at 23,344.25, down 2.35% in the prior session and down 5.64% over five sessions, though up 1.35% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). The Shanghai Composite closed at 3,369.98, down 1.74% over five sessions and up 0.72% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). The offshore internet proxy is weaker still: KWEB closed at 35.17 USD, down 7.03% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25), and the CSI 300 ETF ASHR at 26.87 USD is down 2.64% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Bloomberg reports signs of rotation from small caps to large in Chinese stocks [[n1269]]. USD/CNY sits at 7.2530, up 0.28% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25), so the currency is not signalling stress.
New / Most Important

The signal that matters most comes from China’s own tech leader. Alibaba’s chairman Joe Tsai warned of a bubble in the AI data-centre buildout [[n1339]] and said some AI bets, such as excess data centres, are speculative [[n1340]]. Reuters reports Alibaba is restarting hiring and sees signs of the start of an AI bubble in the US [[n1337]]. Ant Group’s claim that local GPUs cut AI model training costs by 20% [[n1342]] points to cost deflation in the sector. The tension for Chinese equities is that the policy upgrades are real, but the best-known private AI voice is warning about overbuilding, which argues against chasing the rally.
Playbook ✓

Stay Mixed. Prefer large-cap, policy-exposed names and the consumption theme over offshore internet and small caps until the Hang Seng holds its 20-session reference close of 23,034.02. The call turns Bullish if new loans and retail sales keep improving and the factory print holds above 50. It turns Bearish if the factory reading slips below 50 while the Hang Seng loses its reference level. ⚠ Divergence: the Morgan Stanley target raise [[n1369]] and the WSJ growth upgrades [[n1351]] point up, while the Hang Seng is down 5.64% over five sessions and KWEB is down 7.03% over the same span.

geo.label: tightening into tariff risk
parts: Macro Stance

Japan is tightening into a tariff shock. The BOJ kept rates steady and warned of Trump tariff risks [[n4654]], yet core inflation at 3% in February keeps alive bets on a rate hike [[n4699]]. The yield signal is clear: Japan’s 10-year yield has hit a 16½-year high [[n4791]], and Governor Ueda has said the BOJ has been gradually tapering its long-term JGB holdings [[n4747]]. Households feel the squeeze, slashing cash at a record pace as inflation bites [[n4733]]. Toyota, the bellwether exporter, was bullish on Trump until the tariff threats arrived [[n4779]].
Activity & Currency

USD/JPY closed at 150.7740, up 0.73% in the prior session and up 0.61% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). The yen has weakened even as a Japanese lawmaker says it is undervalued and wants steps to reverse outflows [[n4792]]. The Nikkei 225 closed at 37,780.54, up 1.03% over five sessions but down 2.57% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Chip tooling faces a new challenger, with China’s SiCarrier emerging against ASML and other chip-tool titans [[n4754]], and Tokyo Electron is down 12.36% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). SoftBank is still spending into AI, buying Ampere Computing for $6.5 billion [[n4712]], yet its shares are down 12.32% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25).
Playbook ✓

Underweight yen-sensitive exporters with tariff exposure, and keep the long end of the JGB curve light while the 10-year sits at a 16½-year high [[n4791]]. Yen longs work only as a hedge. The call turns Mixed if USD/JPY closes back under its 20-session reference of 149.86 and the Nikkei reclaims its 20-session reference of 38,776.94. It turns Bullish on Japanese equities only if the tapering and the rate-hike bets stop pushing yields up faster than earnings can absorb.

geo.label: soft landing claimed, housing policy active
parts: Macro Stance

Australia is describing a soft landing. ABC reports the budget papers say the economy is on track for a ‘soft landing’ [[n0421]], and the federal budget leans on households, with Centrelink support for 460,000 pensioners in a $450 million move [[n0407]]. Public employment is still growing, with Labor adding 3,400 public service roles [[n0423]], even as a clothing retailer’s collapse cost hundreds of jobs [[n0409]] and a university cut up to 180 more jobs as student visa changes bite [[n0394]].
Demand & Financing

AUD/USD closed at 0.6286, down 1.51% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). The S&P/ASX 200 closed at 7,942.50, up 1.04% over five sessions but down 3.75% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Banks are the swing. CBA closed at 148.63 AUD, down 3.66% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25), and an S&P Global piece says the stock may drop 23% as analysts flag overvaluation [[n0354]]. Housing support is coming through policy: the government is expanding a first-home-buyer scheme as an election looms [[n0328]], and Labor will lift the income and price caps [[n0339]]. On the resource side, iron ore miners are in the spotlight as Chinese demand rises [[n0379]], while BHP closed at 39.04 AUD, down 3.15% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25).
Playbook ✓

Stay Mixed. Fund any rally with resource names that confirm the iron-ore bid rather than with the big banks, which look stretched on the analyst warning [[n0354]]. CBA would need to reclaim its 20-session reference of 154.27 AUD before the bank call turns Bullish. Keep AUD exposure hedged until AUD/USD recovers through its 20-session reference of 0.6338. The call turns Bullish if the ASX 200 holds its five-session gain and the Help to Buy changes [[n0339]] start to show up in housing demand.

geo.label: banks, energy and defence lead; growth soft
parts: Macro Stance

Poland’s central bank is cautious and divided. Money.pl reports the NBP votes show Glapiński cannot count on unanimity [[n5387]], and Parkiet says the NBP sees inflation within target by mid-2026 while the market expects that much sooner [[n5166]]. The NBP is also adding to its reserves, with more tonnes of gold in the vault [[n5313]]. Activity is soft. Industrial output fell 2.0% year on year in February, according to GUS [[n5279]], and ING expects output to recover more slowly than forecast [[n5256]]. Household incomes keep rising [[n5277]], and unemployment is up, though fewer people are out of work than estimated, Business Insider Polska reports [[n5426]]. Dozens of firms announced group layoffs in a single month, TVN24 reports [[n5472]]. The finance ministry relays that Moody’s credited the strong dynamics of the Polish economy and better relations with the EU [[n5310]].
Markets

Polish equities have run hard over 20 sessions. The WIG20 total-return tracker closed at 53.18 PLN, up 8.84% over 20 sessions, and the EPOL ETF closed at 29.11 USD, up 12.18% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Leadership sits in banks and energy: PKO Bank Polski at 78.70 PLN is up 14.16% over 20 sessions, Orlen at 69.90 PLN is up 15.25%, and mBank at 864.20 PLN is up 18.22% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). LPP, the apparel retailer, is down 0.39% over 20 sessions at 17,980.00 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25), so the consumer names have not joined the rally. USD/PLN closed at 3.8639, down 2.43% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25), so the zloty has firmed. The WIG20 is attacking 2800 points [[n5464]], and the index is being reshaped toward consumer names [[n5331]]. Bankier reports that capital on the Warsaw exchange has reached levels it had never seen before [[n5238]].
Fiscal & Politics

Fiscal pressure is the policy risk. Business Insider Polska reports public debt has broken another barrier [[n5292]], and the 2024 budget outturn showed Belka-tax revenue rising [[n5240]]. Banks are the revenue target. Rzeczpospolita asks whether banks, the budget’s golden-egg hen, should be taxed even more [[n5425]], and Money.pl reports the minister wants to get at the banks’ windfall while the sector protests [[n5342]]. The government has also approved a bill to boost spending on social housing [[n4871]]. The ratings backdrop is the offset: the finance ministry says Moody’s appreciated the economy’s strength [[n5310]].
Corporate & Sectors

Banks, energy and defence lead the corporate story. The Warsaw Stock Exchange’s core profit rose on record revenue growth, Reuters reports [[n4911]], and Alior Bank has set out a strategy to 2027 [[n5423]]. Bank dividends for 2025 are being listed [[n5413]]. PGE plans large storage spending, with a headline calling the Żarnowiec project the largest in Europe [[n5381]], and PGE closed at 8.29 PLN, up 17.59% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Orlen is hunting for gas and oil overseas, which Bankier calls practically unlimited resources [[n5448]], and Orlen has received 1.7 billion zloty of European Investment Bank funding for grid development [[n5273]]. CD Projekt says The Witcher 4 will come after 2026 [[n5418]], and the shares closed at 229.70 PLN, up 5.76% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). KGHM is spending billions on new mine shafts [[n5258]], with the stock at 140.75 PLN, up 5.83% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25).
Geopolitics & Security

Defence is the growth story that policy keeps reinforcing. Bankier reports the defence industry is hiring heavily [[n5186]], Money.pl says the sector is trying to widen a production bottleneck [[n5299]], and the state defence group wants to win abroad [[n5225]]. Poland has asked NATO to raise the minimum defence spending to 3% of GDP [[n4816]], Donald Tusk has announced military training for all men [[n4815]], and Poland and the Baltic states plan to quit the landmine treaty over Russia fears [[n4841]]. On Ukraine, Russia and Ukraine agreed a naval ceasefire in the Black Sea [[n4276]], but Moscow set far-reaching conditions for implementing it [[n4246]]. The regional security premium stays on, which keeps defence-linked names in favour.
New / Most Important

The signal that matters most is that the zloty is strong while the factory side is weak. The zloty hit a 10-year high against the dollar on a hawkish central bank in late February [[n4810]], and USD/PLN closed at 3.8639 in the prior session, down 2.43% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). That gives the NBP room to keep policy restrictive while output falls 2.0% year on year [[n5279]]. For equities, rate-sensitive banks carry the rally, and the bank tax debate [[n5425]] is the risk that could reverse that leadership.
Playbook ✓

Stay Bullish on banks, energy and defence, but size bank exposure through the WIG20 total-return tracker rather than one name, because the tax debate [[n5342]] can move quickly. Keep the zloty long only while USD/PLN stays under its 20-session reference of 3.9599. Dino Polska at 455.80 PLN, down 7.19% over five sessions, is the consumer-side warning. The call turns Mixed if the bank tax moves from debate into legislation, or if inflation tracks the market’s earlier timetable rather than the NBP’s mid-2026 view [[n5166]]. ⚠ Divergence: the WIG20 is attacking 2800 [[n5464]] and the zloty is firm, while industrial output fell 2.0% year on year in February [[n5279]].
Narrative

Technology is the consensus AI trade, but the group is running into valuation fatigue. XLK closed at 218.35, up 2.92% over five sessions and down 4.45% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Morgan Stanley’s Mike Wilson sees beaten-up megacap names as the near-term winners [[n5796]], which is a rotation call inside tech rather than a call on the whole sector.
Reported

Micron’s print was solid, but the stock fell: Barron’s says the detail that overshadowed the results pulled shares lower [[n0453]]. MU closed at 94.18 USD, down 7.41% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Nvidia’s earnings beat drew a shrug from investors, S&P Global reports [[n2704]], so beats are not being rewarded at the top of the group.
EPS Upside Watch

Broadcom has the most demand momentum among the chip names, with Forbes asking how high the AI boom can take the chipmaker [[n2646]]. AVGO closed at 188.26 USD, down 7.05% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25), so an upside surprise would have a low bar to clear on price.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention says AI capex is a supercycle, but the loudest voice from China’s largest cloud and commerce group warns of bubble risk. Alibaba’s chairman says there are signs of an AI bubble forming in the US [[n1337]] and warned of a bubble in the AI data-centre buildout [[n1339]]. Quantum-computing stocks are falling as Jensen Huang and other CEOs temper expectations [[n5669]]. The sector’s 20-session drawdown is the market already pricing that doubt.
Narrative

Communication services is holding up on the platform and advertising story. XLC closed at 99.94, up 4.20% over five sessions and down 1.72% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Meta is weighing a paid, ad-free option in the UK [[n2592]], a sign the platform is testing new revenue streams, and Google is searching for an answer to ChatGPT [[n2582]], which keeps the AI-competition debate at the centre of the group.
Reported
The sector’s news is deal flow: Google’s $32 billion Wiz deal may signal a turning point for slow IPO and M&A markets, CNBC reports [[n3469]].
EPS Upside Watch

The watch is on advertising-linked platforms and on the deal pipeline. GOOGL closed at 170.56 USD, up 6.16% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25), and the Wiz deal is the cleanest catalyst for upside in estimates if integration costs stay contained.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention says a slowing ad market hurts platforms, yet Alphabet is up 6.16% over five sessions while the group is still lower over 20. Cathie Wood’s sale of Meta shares for the first time in nearly a year [[n5505]] is a reminder that even long-term holders trim platform names when the story gets crowded. The tension is between the five-session bounce and the 20-session drift.
Narrative

Financials are carried by the curve and by deal flow. The curve is positively sloped with a 10Y-2Y spread of +35 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-25), which supports net interest margins as it steepens. XLF closed at 50.43, up 2.86% over five sessions and down 1.04% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Bloomberg reports banks are preparing a €2.5 billion bond sale for Flutter’s Italy deal [[n3452]], a sign the debt market is open for large transactions.
Reported

Morgan Stanley is cutting 2,000 jobs but sparing its wealth managers, Barron’s reports [[n9833]], which is a cost story rather than a revenue one. MS closed at 125.20 USD, up 6.00% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Axos Financial topped the 2024 ranking of US public banks over $10B in assets, S&P Global reports [[n2642]].
EPS Upside Watch

The upside is in trading and capital-markets revenue after a volatile stretch. JPMorgan closed at 251.13 USD, up 6.88% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25), and Goldman Sachs at 585.94 USD, up 6.19% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25), so some of the rebound is already in the price. The advisory side is the laggard: billions raised by perennially private firms keep IPOs on ice [[n3453]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention says banks lose when recession fears rise, yet the big banks are up more than 6% over five sessions while the sector is still lower over 20. The policy risk cuts across the trade: Semafor reports Treasury’s play for regulatory control puts it on a collision course with the Fed [[n10400]].
Narrative

Energy is trading the Venezuela tariff threat against a Russia-Ukraine truce. XLE closed at 93.23, up 2.07% over five sessions and up 4.00% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Reuters says oil prices are mixed as the Russia-Ukraine truce offsets Venezuela supply worries [[n4251]], and WTI closed at 69.00 USD, up 3.14% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25).
Reported

Sinopec’s full-year profit slumped as headwinds mounted, Bloomberg reports [[n1306]], and Shell plans more cost and spending cuts while handing its chief executive a bigger bonus [[n2684]]. XOM closed at 116.59 USD, up 6.25% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25), so the majors have held up better than the reports suggest.
EPS Upside Watch

The upside is in the cost-cutting majors and in refiners that benefit from wider margins. The cleanest way to be wrong is a Russian supply deal. Traders say the route back for Russian energy is long [[n4303]], which limits how much sanction relief can add to earnings in the near term.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention is that Venezuela tariffs lift crude. Reuters reports Venezuelan oil loadings are slowing amid US tariffs and a licence termination [[n4249]], and China’s purchases have stalled after the tariff threat [[n4193]]. That is a supply squeeze on paper that has not yet shown up as a price surge: WTI is up 3.14% over five sessions but barely changed over 20.
Narrative

Industrials are a defence-and-infrastructure story with a tariff hangover. XLI closed at 134.49, up 1.98% over five sessions and down 0.32% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Germany’s landmark spending bill has won final backing [[n3074]], and chip companies have filed €6 billion of subsidy requests in Germany [[n3061]], a signal for European capex rather than an order book.
Reported

Boeing is cutting jobs in India, a headline says [[n9987]], even as its defence side wins: WSJ reports Boeing gets a lifeline in a Pentagon deal to build the most expensive jet fighter ever [[n8019]]. BA closed at 182.59 USD, up 13.01% over five sessions and up 2.42% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25).
EPS Upside Watch

The upside is in defence procurement and in European suppliers moving into defence. German suppliers are exploring defence opportunities, Automotive News reports [[n2663]], and private-equity defence investment is surging in early 2025, S&P Global says [[n1203]]. Those are demand signals rather than estimate revisions, so the earnings case depends on contract timing.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention says defence is the safe industrial, but Lockheed Martin is down 5.80% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25) while Boeing is up 13.01%. The market is separating the names that win contracts from those carrying legacy costs. Anduril’s plan for a UK drone factory [[n3059]] shows new entrants chasing the same European budgets.
Narrative

Discretionary is where tariffs and confidence meet. XLY closed at 205.92, up 6.42% over five sessions but down 4.86% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25), a bounce inside a downtrend. Business Insider says consumer sentiment is plunging [[n8070]], and retailers are bulking up inventories to blunt the tariff impact [[n0470]], which defers the price pain rather than removing it.
Reported

Nike expects sales will plunge in the current quarter as it faces tariffs and sliding consumer confidence [[n9905]], and its stock fell as the company joined what Fortune calls a growing list of tariff casualties [[n9960]]. NKE closed at 66.54 USD, down 9.23% over five sessions and down 18.58% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Kingfisher’s shares dived on a subdued profit outlook [[n2668]].
EPS Upside Watch

Upside is hard to find. The discretionary names with positive momentum have specific catalysts: Tesla’s rebound on Musk’s return [[n5945]] and Carvana testing new-vehicle sales in Arizona [[n9876]]. The EPS watch is about pricing power, and Nike’s guidance is the cautionary example of what tariffs do to it.
⚡ Breaking Convention

earnings_pattern.title: Earnings Pattern — The Market Pays for Outlook, Not for the Quarter
parts: Rewarded

Guidance that clears the bar is still rewarded, mostly in names with a clear growth story. Aeva’s stock rallied after a fourth-quarter beat and better-than-expected guidance, and retail turned bullish [[n5579]]. Surf Air Mobility rose after hours on upbeat fourth-quarter revenue [[n5573]]. Those are small-cap reactions.
Punished

Beats with soft outlooks and guidance cuts are punished. Micron’s stock fell after earnings, as the detail that overshadowed the strong results pulled the shares lower [[n0453]]; MU closed at 94.18 USD, down 7.41% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Nike expects sales to plunge in the current quarter [[n9905]], and NKE closed at 66.54 USD, down 18.58% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). McCormick missed quarterly profit estimates on higher expenses [[n2687]], Kingfisher’s shares dived on a subdued profit outlook [[n2668]], and KB Home cut its outlook as consumer confidence fell [[n10012]].
Pattern

The pattern is that outlook is what gets paid for. A beat that a single detail overshadows is punished (Micron), a guide-down is punished hardest (Nike, Kingfisher), and a small-cap beat with a raised outlook is rewarded (Aeva). Nvidia’s beat drew a shrug from investors [[n2704]], which is the same message at the top of the market: when the stock is already priced for the next leg, the quarter is no longer the catalyst. The reports that carry outlook cuts all come from consumer-exposed or tariff-exposed businesses, which is consistent with a sentiment index at a four-year low [[n10100]].
Attention into EPS

Attention into the next prints is on tariffs and the consumer. Options traders are positioning ahead of Chewy’s earnings call [[n5939]], which trades the guide more than the headline. EPS upside is most credible where estimates have already been cut, so the watch is on guidance language rather than on the quarter’s reported figure.
Playbook

Own the names whose guidance is being raised into the next print and avoid those whose guide is cut, because the market pays for outlook more than for the quarter. Hedge consumer-discretionary exposure with puts on the names where a guide-down has already cost 18.58% over 20 sessions, and let the stronger names lead. The call turns Bullish on the group if beats come with raised guidance, as Aeva’s did, and turns Bearish if a beat overshadowed by one detail gets the same reaction Micron did.

flows.title: Capital Flows & Liquidity Framework — Caution at the Central Banks, Rotation in the Tape

The Bank of England kept its rate at 4.5% [[n2976]], while warning that global trade uncertainty has intensified [[n2983]]. The money is rotating. Stock investors are starting to shift money from the US to Europe [[n3175]], and the WSJ says investors who were all in on US stocks are looking elsewhere [[n3104]]. In ETFs, bond funds are in demand as investors flee the Nasdaq QQQ, CNBC reports [[n3518]], and QQQ closed at 493.46 USD, down 3.87% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Liquidity is adequate, but the marginal flow is into bonds and out of megacap tech, and leveraged products are the weak point. Hold duration in the belly rather than the long end, keep leveraged ETFs out of core books, and prefer European exposure, where the money is moving [[n3175]]. anticipatory.title: A Fed that will not cut quickly

The risk is that a politically driven cut lifts inflation expectations. Former Cleveland Fed President Loretta Mester warned that tariffs could disrupt inflation expectations [[n10233]]. In that case the long end sells off and the steepener works for the wrong reason, with losses in the long-duration leg.

anticipatory.title: ECB and the German fiscal pivot

Conditional Expression

If spreads widen, reduce the periphery exposure and keep the German names that stand to gain from the spending; chip companies have filed €6 billion of subsidy requests in Germany [[n3061]].
Risk

The risk is a policy turn: a rate decision that reads as tighter, or a capital-rule change that reads as looser bank requirements, would move bank and sovereign spreads together, and the German trade would lose its funding source.

FCX closed at 43.01 USD, up 7.96% over five sessions and up 17.00% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). The hurdle is the 20-session reference of 36.76 USD. The risk is a tariff reversal: if the bets unwind, the front-month copper price, at 5.18 USD per lb, gives back the premium first (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25).
Trade Expression
Long FCX or COPX as the equity expression, with the metal future as the pure one. Invalidation: copper closes below its 20-session reference of 4.49 USD per lb.

catalysts.title: $LLY — the pill data

Buy LLY calls ahead of the readout, or a call spread with the upper strike at the 901.80 reference. Invalidation: the stock failing to hold its five-session gain after the data.

retail.title: Strategy / MSTR — the copycats move into bitcoin
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The crowd's story is that a bitcoin treasury is bitcoin with a stock ticker attached, and now the copies are arriving. GameStop, a meme stock, says it will invest corporate cash in bitcoin the way MicroStrategy does [[n1798]]. Metaplanet has added 150 bitcoin to its tally, days after Eric Trump's adviser appointment [[n1698]], and the simple reading is: buy the company that holds the coin, and the coin does the rest. The stock itself is the number holders tend to watch: it closed at 341.81 USD, well above where it stood twenty sessions ago (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25).
What Is Driving It

The hard evidence is in the tape. Strategy closed at 341.81 USD, up 1.81% in the prior session, up 20.70% over five sessions and up 36.45% over 20, against a reference close of 250.51 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). Bitcoin is not carrying the move. BTC-USD closed at 87,471.70 USD, up 3.93% over five sessions but down 3.48% over 20 against 90,623.56 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-25). The proxies are running harder than the coin: MARA is up 18.06% over five sessions and 14.73% over 20, and Coinbase is up 12.75% over five. The catalyst is the copycat headline. CNBC reports that GameStop shares soared 12% after the bitcoin plan [[n1798]], and Metaplanet's 150-bitcoin addition is dated March 24 [[n1698]]. Across assets, the S&P 500 is up 2.89% over five sessions, the Nasdaq 100 is up 4.13%, and the VIX has fallen to 17.15, down 20.97% over the same span (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25), so the backdrop is a rising tide.
The Social Signal

The attention runs through the comparisons on offer. CoinDesk's March 25 piece weighs the two Strategy preferred issues, STRF against STRK [[n1811]], which is the retail question of which instrument to own. Forbes asks what the correlation between BTC and MSTR is [[n1833]], the question a crowd asks when the stock has moved further than the coin. Yahoo Finance's March 20 headline reports a 16% share surge on a new US$1.24 dividend [[n1509]], and TradingView's March 23 headline says Saylor hints at an impending bitcoin purchase after a capital raise [[n1607]]. Each one invites the same reading: hold the stock as a levered way to own the coin, and let the treasury do the buying.
Historical Analog

This is a familiar pattern from meme episodes. A name the crowd already knows becomes the vehicle for one simple idea it can repeat. Then the crowd arrives after the stock has already moved, buying the story rather than any change in the numbers. GameStop's plan is the copy in this case: a meme name copying a treasury model, and a copy is easier to repeat than the original. The mechanism that matters is the wrapper. A stock that holds bitcoin can rise faster than the coin on the way up, so late buyers can end up holding the premium rather than the asset.
Smart Money View

Institutions split on the coin and on the stock. Standard Chartered's March 24 headline says bitcoin could replace Tesla in the Magnificent 7 to boost returns and reduce volatility [[n1631]], which is the bull case for holding the asset at all. Monness Crespi Hardt started Strategy at Neutral and puts fair value at $200 a share [[n1431]], the skeptic's number to set against a stock that closed at 341.81 USD. The disagreement is about price, not direction: the bulls are valuing the coin, while the skeptics question the premium the stock charges above it.
When the Narrative Breaks

The levels matter here. The stock's 20-session reference is 250.51, and a close back under it would erase the 36.45% gain. Bitcoin is the tell: BTC-USD closed at 87,471.70 USD, still under its 90,623.56 reference, so the treasury premium is paying for a coin that has not recovered. A reclaim of 90,623.56 would show the coin catching up with the stock, and a further fall in bitcoin would hit the holdings and the equity together. The financing is the risk to watch. CoinDesk's comparison of the preferred issues [[n1811]] matters because preferred stock is a claim that ranks ahead of the common shares, so each new issue adds to the layer above the equity. The instrument risk is the premium itself, which can compress faster than the coin falls.

retail.title: Ether / ETH — the network is busy, the price is not
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The crowd's case for ether is the network. Yahoo Finance's March 20 headline says Ethereum dominates the stablecoin market with $850 billion in monthly volume, led by USDC and USDT [[n1499]]. The bullish reading is that the chain which dominates stablecoin volume should have the stronger price, and that is the bullish line. It makes the lag hard to accept, because the network is working and the price is not.
Where It Breaks

The lag is in the price. ETH-USD closed at 2,067.76 USD, down 7.77% over 20 sessions against a reference of 2,241.98 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-25). The ether fund, iShares Ethereum Trust, closed at 15.72 USD, down 16.52% over 20 sessions against 18.83 USD, though its five-session bounce of 9.24% is the crowd's case for buying again. Yahoo Finance's March 21 headline says analysts cite inflationary problems, the Dencun upgrade blowback and Solana's meme coins [[n1574]]. The break is in the flows: TradingView, citing CoinShares, reports that XRP and Solana lead altcoin ETP inflows as Ethereum slumps [[n1744]]. A close back above 2,241.98 would show the price closing the gap, and a flow ranking that flips back to ether would show the crowd returning. The instrument risk is that an ether fund carries the coin's full volatility with no offset.

retail.title: Advanced Micro Devices / AMD — the 10x Radeon claim
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The story is that AMD is the challenger that is finally winning. CNBC's March 20 headline says Lisa Su has already vanquished Intel and is going after Nvidia [[n2390]]. On March 25 the number that travelled was the claim that RX 9070 XT sales are 10x higher than all previous Radeon generations [[n2639]], repeated in a second headline that calls the launch the best in Radeon history [[n7925]]. A gaming card becomes a stock story, and the crowd keeps the 10x and tends to drop the caveat.
Where It Breaks

The break is the caveat: the 10x figure is for the first week of availability [[n2639]]. AMD closed at 114.81 USD, up 0.84% in the prior session and 10.92% over five sessions, with a 20-session gain of 10.44% against a reference of 103.96 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). That reference is the level to watch, because a close back under it would erase the 20-session recovery. The rebound is stock-specific: the semiconductor ETF SOXX is down 4.68% over 20 sessions and Nvidia is down 4.69% over the same span (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). The instrument risk is that a single chip name still moves with the sector, so a sector break would take the Radeon story down with it.

retail.title: Tesla / TSLA — the comeback still rests on Musk
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The catalysts are unchanged: a tariff leeway that Reuters calls possible [[n5833]], and Musk's all-hands call to hang on [[n6973]] [[n7033]]. Fortune's March 25 headline has a Tesla analyst saying the chief executive is back in charge and that investors are rewarding the stock [[n5945]]. TradingView describes a retail buying frenzy on market optimism [[n5876]], and Bloomberg has Cathie Wood sticking with a $2,600 target [[n5884]]. The number on the table is the target, not the price.
Where It Breaks

TSLA closed at 288.14 USD, up 3.50% in the prior session and 27.89% over five sessions, but still down 4.84% over 20 against a reference of 302.80 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-25). A close back under 288.14 would show the rebound stalling, and a reclaim of 302.80 would turn the 20-session picture positive. The hard data keeps pointing the other way: Reuters reports that Tesla's sales and market share in Europe dropped again in February [[n8372]], and The Guardian says Europe sales dropped nearly 45% amid the row over Musk's Trump links [[n8373]]. The instrument risk is high beta: a stock that has moved 27.89% in five sessions can reverse just as fast.
